mcqs.question: What is the key structural difference between how Grid and Flexbox arrange items?
options: Grid only supports fixed pixel sizes; Flexbox is the only model with proportional units
Flexbox requires naming every item; Grid places items automatically with no way to name regions
Grid can only create a single row or column, same as Flexbox, just with different property names
Grid declares the row/column structure up front and items slot into it, while Flexbox distributes items along one axis based on their content and grow/shrink values
mcqs.explanation: Grid's defining trait is that the structure — tracks, lines, areas — exists before items are placed into it, which is what lets rows and columns align across the whole layout. Flexbox has no predefined structure; it arranges items along a single axis, and both models support fr/flex proportional units.

mcqs.question: What does `grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(200px, 1fr));` produce?
options: As many 200px-minimum columns as fit the container, stretching evenly to fill any remaining width
Exactly one column that is always 200px wide regardless of container size
A fixed number of columns set by the auto-fit keyword, ignoring container width
Columns that shrink below 200px once the container gets narrow enough
mcqs.explanation: auto-fit computes how many minmax(200px, 1fr) tracks fit the current container width and stretches them to consume the rest, which is exactly the mechanism behind responsive card grids with zero media queries. minmax's lower bound of 200px is a floor the tracks won't shrink past, and auto-fit isn't a fixed column count.

mcqs.question: A grid is defined with three explicit rows, but a dynamic feed sometimes renders a fourth item. What governs the size of that overflow row if `grid-auto-rows` is never set?
options: The overflow item is dropped and not rendered
It reuses the size of the last explicit row automatically
It defaults to `auto`, sizing itself to its own content rather than matching the other rows
The grid throws a layout error and collapses
mcqs.explanation: Rows created in the implicit grid default to auto sizing based on content, unless grid-auto-rows overrides that — which is exactly why a dynamic-count grid can end up with inconsistent row heights if you forget to set it. Nothing about overflow drops content or reuses the previous explicit row's size automatically, and there's no error state for this.

mcqs.question: A navbar needs its links spaced evenly in a single row that occasionally wraps on small screens. Which layout model fits best, and why?
options: Grid, because it's the newer and generally more capable model
Flexbox, because the layout is fundamentally one axis — a row of items — even though it can wrap
Neither — this specific case requires floats for correct wrapping behavior
Grid, because grid-template-columns can size columns individually per item
mcqs.explanation: The deciding question is dimensionality, not novelty: a navbar is conceptually a single row, which is exactly what Flexbox is built for, wrapping included. Grid could technically do it, but it would mean pre-declaring track counts for a list whose length varies, which is more setup for no real benefit.

mcqs.question: A card grid uses `repeat(auto-fill, minmax(220px, 1fr))` and currently has only two cards, in a container wide enough for four columns. What happens to the two cards?
options: They stay at roughly 220px each, because auto-fill preserves the empty tracks instead of letting real items expand into them
They stretch to fill all four column slots evenly, same as auto-fit would
The grid collapses to a single column since there aren't enough items
auto-fill removes unused tracks entirely, identical to auto-fit's behavior
mcqs.explanation: auto-fill keeps the empty tracks it computed room for, so existing items stay at their minmax size instead of stretching — the opposite of auto-fit, which collapses unused tracks to zero and lets real items expand to fill the freed space. This is the one behavioral difference between the two keywords.

mcqs.question: A team builds a two-dimensional dashboard entirely with nested flex containers, and the row heights keep drifting out of alignment as content changes. What's the underlying issue?
options: flex-wrap was left at its default value of nowrap
The layout genuinely needs cross-axis alignment across multiple lines at once, which is Grid's job, not Flexbox's — nested flex rows don't coordinate with each other
The team forgot to set align-content on the outer container
Flexbox cannot express a two-dimensional layout under any circumstances, even with extra markup
mcqs.explanation: Flexbox's lines don't communicate with each other, so nested flex rows can't guarantee columns line up the way a true grid's tracks do by construction — that's precisely the problem Grid exists to solve. Tweaking flex-wrap or align-content might mask the symptom in specific cases but doesn't address the structural mismatch between the tool and the problem.
